exact_claim: The relevant Rigvedic terminology exists but has not been recognised, because the words that later denote writing carry other senses in the corpus.
attested_or_hypothetical: HYPOTHETICAL — and the only hypothesis in this domain that this session could actually test
chronological_fit: Internal to the corpus. The Arnold stratum of every occurrence is recorded, which is relative chronology; no absolute date is claimed.
geographical_fit: Not applicable: a lexical question inside one corpus.
positive_evidence: Tested and answered in part. Two instruments, a candidate census and a gloss scan of the whole lexicon, converge: the later writing vocabulary is absent (DK-R-002); no lemma is glossed in the writing or sealing field (DK-R-003, DK-R-004); a marking vocabulary is present (DK-R-005); akṣára-, the word that later names a written character, occurs 8 times and denotes a syllable of chanted speech in all eight (DK-R-008); and √rikh- 'to scratch' is present, twice, of Pūṣan's awl and a heart (DK-R-006, DK-R-007).
contrary_evidence: The instruments have a stated blind spot: 296 lemmas carry no gloss, and the passage-level check ran through two translations of one philological tradition (DK-A-003, DEP-021).
independent_support: The candidate census and the gloss scan are independent of each other in construction, though both rest on Grassmann's glosses for the second half.
current_specialist_standing: Not applicable: this is a measurement of a corpus, not a position in a literature.
diagnostic_predictions: If unrecognised terminology existed, a lemma glossed in the marking field would appear with a durable object as its target, or an unglossed lemma would cluster in passages about surfaces and signs.
falsifier: A Rigvedic passage in which a marking or incising verb takes a durable inscribed surface as its object. None was found in 232 occurrences; one would falsify the negative.
proportional_space: The largest allocation in this unit, because it is the only part of §4.K with retrievable evidence on both sides of the question.
reason: Answered in the direction of 'present but doing other work', not 'absent'. The distinction matters: a naive candidate list returns 'the root for write is absent', which is false (DK-R-006).

exact_claim: The Rigvedic silence needs no special explanation, because a liturgical praise corpus would not describe an administrative or graphic technology even if its composers had seen one.
attested_or_hypothetical: HYPOTHETICAL — the null explanation for this domain
chronological_fit: Internal to the corpus; no absolute chronology needed for the genre argument.
positive_evidence: Partial and internal. The corpus records shares, debts, tribute, price and measuring (DK-R-013) but no instrument of standard weight beyond a measuring cord (DK-R-014), and its marking vocabulary attaches to bodies, animals, skies and hearts (DK-R-007, DK-R-010, DK-R-011). That is the profile of a genre that names what the liturgy needs and little else.
contrary_evidence: The genre argument can be made to absorb any absence, which is its weakness. It predicts nothing on its own.
independent_support: The archive audit at APA-K-001 is a separate instrument reaching the same conclusion from the corpus's conditions of production.
current_specialist_standing: The standard caution in Vedic philology; not characterisable from a retrieved source here.
diagnostic_predictions: A genre-based silence predicts that other technologies of comparable visibility are equally absent, and that the absent vocabulary reappears when the genre widens in later strata or later corpora.
falsifier: A Rigvedic description of a comparable non-liturgical technology in detail would weaken it; systematic absence of all such description would strengthen it.
eligible_for_extended_analysis: ELIGIBLE — and it is the null
proportional_space: Small, and it is placed first among the explanations of the silence, because the null is the explanation the others must beat.
reason: §6: 'Unknown' is residual, never a positive rival explanation - and the null here is not 'unknown' but 'the genre would not record it'. It is testable in later Vedic corpora, none of which was reachable in this session.
